title: devex
text:
devex

maria: @here Heads-up — we’re kicking off a cross-org migration for CI and identity next week. Short version: migrate CI workloads off GitHub-hosted runners to the new self-hosted runner fleet (label: redwood-runner) and enable org SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning. Goal: better perf, cost predictability, and centralized access control. Timeline: canary groups start 2026-04-13, org-wide roll 2026-04-27. Action for teams: update workflows and re-authorize Jira/GitHub apps by the roll date. Docs/guides: https://internal.redwood/devex/ci-sso-migration (step-by-step + migration checklist).

josh: do we have an automated migration helper or is this manual per-repo?

maria: There’s a migration helper (script + GH app) that will open a PR with suggested changes for simple workflows. Complex monorepos will need manual review. The helper runs in a dry-run mode first, then can create PRs for you. We’ll assign canary teams to validate the PRs.

devops-bot: scheduled: runner-provisioning job queued for 2026-04-13T03:00:00Z. Will provision 50 runners in us-west initially.

samir: Quick Q — how do we handle secrets? Our workflows use a few long-lived PATs stored as repo secrets.

maria: Replace PATs with OIDC where possible; examples in the guide. For secrets that must remain, move them to the org secrets store and mark as "restricted". If you need help, tag #eng-infra and we’ll assist. Example change: 

```yaml
# old
steps:
  - uses: actions/checkout@v3
  - name: Publish
    env:
      TOKEN: ${{ secrets.PUBLISH_PAT }}
    run: ./deploy.sh

# new (runs on self-hosted + use OIDC / org secrets)
runs-on: [self-hosted, redwood-runner]
steps:
  - uses: actions/checkout@v3
  - name: Publish
    env:
      TOKEN: ${{ secrets.ORG_PUBLISH_TOKEN }}
    run: ./deploy.sh
```

maria: We’ll also rotate repo-level PATs for any repos that don’t migrate by 2026-05-04.

olivia: For SAML enforcement — does this mean MFA will be required for everyone? Any exemptions?

maria: SAML SSO enforcement will require org SSO; MFA requirements follow the IdP policy (Okta). There will be a small exemptions process for service accounts that cannot use SSO; open a support ticket to security with justification. SCIM provisioning will auto-sync groups -> GitHub teams.

lara: What about the Jira integration? We use the old Jira GitHub app and a webhook for PR metadata. Will that break?

maria: Good call — we’re migrating to the new Atlassian Connect integration that supports per-repo install and improved issue linking. Migration will require repo admins to re-authorize the app during the migration window; we’ll detect installs and DM repo admins with a one-click reauth flow. There will be a 7-day grace period where both integrations run in parallel for safety.

josh: Any perf expectations for self-hosted runners? Start/queue times?

samir: We measured median startup ~12s for a warmed runner pool and cold start ~40s. We’ve tuned autoscaling to keep a small warm buffer for popular repos.

maria: Canary plan: 10 teams (infra, devtools, platform, and 7 product teams) on 2026-04-13. If canary looks good we expand to 50% of repos on 2026-04-20 and full roll on 2026-04-27. Opt-out window for non-critical repos closes 2026-04-10.

lara: If my repo needs more time, what’s the process?

maria: Fill out the migration delay form linked in the guide (subject to approval). We’ll triage by impact.

devops-bot: reminder: migration docs updated — https://internal.redwood/devex/ci-sso-migration#checklist (v1.2).

samir: Will there be support office hours?

maria: Yes — daily office hours 10:00-11:00 PT from 2026-04-08 through 2026-04-21 in #devex-help. We’ll also run a live walkthrough recording.

olivia: One last thing — logging/audit for runner usage?

maria: All runner actions will be logged to central audit logs and sent to Splunk for 90 days. We’ll surface anomalous usage as alerts.

josh: Thanks — I’ll start the dry-run for our infra repo and ping if anything breaks.

maria: Thanks everyone — please read the checklist and flag any blockers early. :pray:
